_what: The comparison the hub ruled: direction gate reverted on a scratch branch (a9bf1807, DEBUG only, s4.debug.bin 845594), same leftward circuit at $600 with SUSTAINED held input, against the same fixed ground.
_headline: IT REFUTES MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM. Leftward gives ZERO toggles under BOTH rules, so the direction gate is NOT what broke leftward entry.

instrument_control_FIRST._why: A zero toggle count is ambiguous between 'nothing fired' and 'the ring is stuck'. The ring already held 8 orphaned hits from previous epochs and watchpoint_clear --all does NOT drain them, so the stuck reading was live.
instrument_control_FIRST.method: fresh watchpoint w5, reset, boot 240 frames — boot is known to write Sst.layer
instrument_control_FIRST.result: a NEW w5 hit recorded at seq 8, frame 54, this epoch
instrument_control_FIRST.verdict: RING IS LIVE. The zero readings below are real, not vacuous.
instrument_control_FIRST.note: This control was run BEFORE interpreting any zero. Without it the whole comparison would have been unfalsifiable.

marks_are_intact.gate: tools/loop_crossover_gate.py on the reverted build, EXIT 0
marks_are_intact.meaning: the marks were NOT destroyed by aurora's fill. This rules out the obvious explanation.

what_this_overturns.my_claim: I told the hub 'the direction rule FAILS condition (a) leftward' and 'the direction gate is what broke leftward entry'. The second half is now refuted: leftward does not cross under the plane-keyed rule either.
what_this_overturns.aurora_pre_registration: Their derivation predicted a leftward entrant crosses at the bottom mark BECAUSE the toggle is direction-blind, climbs the right arc on B, and completes. Measured against the reverted gate on this data, it does NOT. The pre-registration is honoured as a real prediction and it did not survive contact.
what_this_overturns.what_DID_change: In the FIRST build of this session (before the ground fill), the same leftward drive DID cross — one toggle at frame 397, x 1151. So the leftward crossing was lost somewhere between that build and this one, and the crossover RULE is not the variable. The remaining candidates are the collision-data changes: aurora's 532-cell fill and/or the crown curve re-bake, both of which renumber the content-addressed attr set.

_not_established: why the leftward crossing was lost. The marks ship and are consumed, so it is not mark destruction. Most likely the player's PATH no longer intersects the mark cell — his trajectory differs on the new ground (he now runs 300px further west unobstructed) — but I have not traced his y against the mark cell's row and will not assert it.
the rightward circuit under the reverted rule. Not driven; my context budget went to the instrument control instead, which was the right trade because without it every number here is worthless.
